news.title: Match report: Chelsea Women 1-0 Paris Saint-Germain
news.body_en: Veerle Buurman's late winner secured a precious 1-0 victory over Paris Saint-Germain at Plough Lane, lifting Chelsea top of the UEFA Women's Champions League league phase table with one match remaining. The Blues dominated possession but found it tough to convert chances against a disciplined PSG backline, but Buurman struck from close range following an 87th-minute corner. Sjoeke Nusken had been denied moments earlier by a magnificent save from Katarzyna Kiedrzynek, whose performance kept PSG level for much of the evening. It was another hard-earned victory for Sonia Bompastor's side, who maintained our unbeaten start to the campaign and recorded a fifth successive clean sheet in the Champions League. The result was significant after two goalless draws with Lyon and Hacken had left us needing a strong finish to the league phase. The Blues had won both European home fixtures this season, but PSG provided a different examination of our attacking patience. Bompastor made three alterations from Saturday's 1-0 Women's Super League victory over Manchester City. Nathalie Bjorn captained the Blues in place of Lucy Bronze, while Buurman replaced Kadeisha Buchanan and Aggie Beever-Jones came in for the injured Melvine Malard. The Blues quickly established control of the contest but found PSG's organised defensive shape difficult to break down. Potter had our first presentable opening in the 10th minute, meeting a corner with a free header but directing her effort wide. PSG suffered an early setback when defender Isabela was forced off injured in the 15th minute, with Olga Carmona replacing her. The visitors nevertheless remained dangerous on the break. Merveille Kanjinga offered their most persistent attacking threat down the right, demanding strong defending from Katie McCabe and the Chelsea backline. At the other end, Beever-Jones found space to meet a delivery with her head but could not direct it toward goal as clear openings remained scarce. Our best first-half opportunity arrived just before the interval. Baltimore's effort was kept out by Kiedrzynek, with Thompson reacting to the rebound but unable to force the loose ball home. Although our midfielders found space to collect the ball, PSG kept numbers behind it and protected the central areas. Bompastor's side were forced into wide deliveries, with Beever-Jones often crowded out before she could turn towards goal. Despite enjoying the majority of possession and registering seven attempts before the break, Chelsea went into half-time without making the breakthrough. PSG, meanwhile, had not forced Hannah Hampton into a save. The visitors offered more attacking ambition after the restart, and Hampton was finally called upon in the 53rd minute when Kanjinga drove towards goal and tested her at the near post. Buurman and Bjorn were alert whenever PSG threatened on the counterattack, while Potter remained composed in midfield as we continued to probe for an opening. Bompastor turned to her substitutes on the hour, introducing Erin Cuthbert, Maika Hamano and Bronze for Wieke Kaptein, Thompson and McCabe. The changes gave Chelsea fresh impetus. Cuthbert's set-piece delivery caused problems for the PSG defence, with Kiedrzynek producing another important stop following a corner. Cuthbert then worked an opening on the edge of the area but was unable to get her shot away cleanly under pressure. PSG almost punished us at the other end when Tara Elimbi Gilbert lifted an effort over the bar after a threatening counterattack involving Kanjinga and 16-year-old substitute Alyssa Charlier. With Cuthbert providing urgency from midfield and sharper deliveries from set-pieces, Chelsea began to find more promising positions. The visitors remained stubborn, however, and it appeared that a single moment might decide this finely balanced encounter. Beever-Jones sent a free-kick over the crossbar before making way for Nisken in the closing stages. The German midfielder made an immediate impression, meeting a delivery with a firm header that looked destined for goal until Kiedrzynek produced an exceptional reaction save. But the resulting corner finally broke PSG's resistance. Cuthbert delivered into the crowded penalty area and, after the ball was not cleared, Buurman reacted sharply at the near post to turn it home in the 87th minute. There was still defending to do, though, and Hampton stood firm as PSG pressed for an equaliser, including a late effort from Mbock. The final whistle confirmed another clean sheet and three valuable European points after a patient and determined display that, until the end, appeared to be heading for a draw. We remain unbeaten after five league-phase matches, with our fate to be decided in the final round. We currently lead the table, with the top four advancing directly into the knockout phase. The Blues visit Liverpool in the WSL on Saturday before concluding the Champions League league phase away to OH Leuven on 16 December. Chelsea: Hampton, Carpenter, Bjorn (c), Buurman, McCabe (Bronze 60), Walsh, Potter, Thompson (Hamano 60), Kaptein (Cuthbert 60), Baltimore, Beever-Jones (Nusken 83). Unused substitutes: Peng, Spencer, Buchanan, Las, Dragoni, Brown. Goalscorer: Buurman 87. Booked: Bronze 89. Paris Saint-Germain: Kiedrzynek, Isabela (Carmona 15), Mbock (c), Samoura, Elimbi Gilbert, Echegini (Morissaint 90), Groenen, Osteras, Le Guilly, Feller (Charlier 68), Kanjinga. news.title: Cuthbert taking confidence from team-mates’ quality for ‘proper Champions League night’
news.body_en: Erin Cuthbert can’t wait for another big night in the UEFA Women’s Champions League when Chelsea host Paris Saint-Germain at Plough Lane, and called on her fellow Blues to show their quality once again to follow up a crucial win over Manchester City with another in Europe. Chelsea defeated Man City in a top-of-the-table Women’s Super League clash at Stamford Bridge on Saturday to go clear in first place in the table. Now, attention shifts just down the road to Plough Lane, where we are hoping to do the same in the Champions League. With both teams within striking distance of the automatic qualification places in the league phase – just one goal away in Chelsea’s case – captain Cuthbert is anticipating a mouthwatering tie when Paris Saint-Germain come to west London. ‘I honestly relish playing these games,’ said the midfielder. ‘As a football player you want to be playing in the biggest games under the lights in Wimbledon, so we're really excited by the opportunity. ‘I love playing against the top clubs. They always bring a good away support as well that will create a good atmosphere. So it will feel like a proper Champions League night.’ Cuthbert is also going into the game full of confidence in Chelsea’s ability, with the Blues remaining unbeaten in the Champions League and yet to concede a goal in the league phase, having picked up maximum points from our home games so far. ‘I get a lot of my confidence from looking around me, looking at the quality of players that we have,’ she continued. ‘I think you saw over the course of the season the amount of goal scorers that have chipped in across the season. As an opponent, that's really difficult to defend against, knowing that everyone can chip in with goals. They can come from different places, so I think that's really important. ‘But we've got a really good team camaraderie. Everyone's encouraging each other. I think even against Hacken, when the goal wasn't coming, you could see the urgency, but with calm. That's important, that we show a little bit of urgency because we want to score goals, but we do it in a calm and composed manner. ‘Everybody's been so good and I think it's the resilience in the squad. You can see that everybody is up for the fight and up for the battle. Whenever there's tough times, everybody just puts their head down and keeps working. ‘The work ethic and the work rate and intensity that we've been going at this season has been really impressive. Nobody's willing to stop and we're all trying to one-up each other on how much we can do. That's only going to push the squad to new heights.’ Our skipper won’t be underestimating the size of the challenge that awaits on Wednesday evening though, knowing we face a Paris Saint-Germain side with plenty of quality of their own, as well as being determined to bounce back from a defeat to Bayern Munich last time out – their first of the current campaign. ‘They've had a little bit of a difficult start in terms of who they've played opponent-wise, but everybody knows the quality of PSG,’ Cuthbert concluded. ‘They've been one of the top clubs in Europe for as long as I can remember and as long as I've been at Chelsea. ‘I've played them many times, had some late moments against PSG as well. They'll be wanting to pick up points. It's been a tough run for them, so I'm sure they'll be hungry. If I was in that dressing room and we've not had the start that we wanted, I would be making sure that everybody's up for the game tonight. So I'm expecting a tough one. ‘But I'm expecting us to be on it, and that's the beauty of it. We played Manchester City on Saturday, but we have to go again. That performance means nothing unless we back it up tonight.’

news.title: The final preparations
Internationals: Martinez returns and Anselmino debuts in huge Argentina win
news.body_en: Several Chelsea players were involved as our South American contingent brought this international window to a close, including record-equalling Emiliano Martinez and Aaron Anselmino returning from injury as captain and debutant for Argentina. Argentina are beginning their post-Lionel Messi era in earnest during this break, having bid farewell to their legendary skipper and talisman last month. After losing to Uruguay last week, they were looking to kick-start things with a friendly against Costa Rica in the early hours of Wednesday morning UK time. With Messi no longer involved, manager Lionel Scaloni handed Martinez the captain’s armband, as the experienced goalkeeper made his first appearance since undergoing surgery on a fractured jaw suffered in Chelsea’s 2-0 win at Everton a month ago. Fellow Blues Anselmino and Valentin Barco were among the Argentina substitutes, as the Albiceleste wasted no time asserting their dominance by taking the lead inside the opening 10 minutes. By half-time they were four goals up, and added another shortly after the break. With 20 minutes remaining, Scaloni called on Anselmino from the bench, handing the young defender his first senior appearance for his country – and his first appearance of the campaign after suffering a thigh injury in pre-season. Two more goals followed to give Argentina an emphatic 7-0 victory, ending their November international window on a high. It was also the 47th clean sheet of Martinez's international career, on his 71st cap, matching Sergio Romero's all-time Argentina record. Ecuador were also in action on Wednesday morning as they hosted Bolivia and recorded their second 2-0 win of this break, having already defeated Costa Rica by the same scoreline. Moises Caicedo captained his country from the start before being withdrawn at half-time with their two-goal lead already secured. Teenager Kendry Paez came off the bench for the final 25 minutes.

news.title: OTD: Classic Match | West Brom 0-4 Chelsea
Juan Mata retires: Forward's lifelong bonds to Chelsea and London
news.body_en: With the news Juan Mata has announced his retirement, we revisit an interview we conducted with the Spaniard a few years ago, in which he reflects on his love affair with this club and this city that will leave him forever grateful for the time he spent at Stamford Bridge... Mata was part of a close-knit quartet of Spaniards who formed lasting friendships at Chelsea. It was on 22 August 2011 that Chelsea and Valencia agreed a deal for the playmaker to leave his homeland. In the years since, he has taken in further spells at Manchester United, Galatasaray, Vissel Kobe and now Western Sydney Wanderers. He has established himself as a fan favourite at every club, in part for his performances, personality and creative style of play, but also because he has embraced the life and culture of each club's respective city. The regular blog he wrote during his time at Chelsea was devoted equally to updates on his football career and his travels exploring London, full of his own photography. Yes, he was a great player for the Blues. But more than that, he became one of us, an adopted Londoner who felt the pulse of the club and the city. ‘I like that and I always try to do the same,’ he explained. ‘I did the same in Turkey, in Istanbul, which is an incredible city, and in Japan. I find it important to get to know my surroundings, the culture and the history around the city where I live. ‘I feel very privileged to have had the opportunity to live in London, in Manchester, in Istanbul, in Japan and Australia. I’m getting to know different cultures, different vibes of cities, and I’ve tried to embrace it as much as I can.’ There’s no question Mata has achieved a rare balance in his life. You only have to look at the success and longevity of his career, still playing top-flight football at the age of 37, to know he is a dedicated professional. But he is also aware there is more to life and happiness than football. Of course, that doesn’t mean the sport he loves isn’t a great source of pride and pleasure for him. How could it not be for someone who has had so many career highs, prime among them his time at Stamford Bridge. His first season with Chelsea was one that has gone down in history. In 2012, Mata couldn’t stop winning. He made more appearances than any other outfield Chelsea player as the trophies began to arrive in quick succession in 2011/12 – and Mata was at the heart of things. He netted in the 5-1 thrashing of rivals Tottenham Hotspur in the FA Cup semi-final, a competition we would win. He scored the crucial away goal in the UEFA Champions League last 16 against Napoli that made our famous comeback at Stamford Bridge possible. And he provided the perfect assist for Didier Drogba to equalise in the final as we became the first London club to be crowned European champions. Like Fernando Torres, Mata wasn’t finished there - both of Chelsea’s representatives in the Spanish national team found the net to help their country beat Italy 4-0 in the 2012 UEFA European Championship final. ‘Fernando was in the same situation as me,’ Juan reflected thoughtfully. ‘The good thing is that when you win and enjoy it so much, there is a point it seems like winning is all there is. That is the problem. When you don’t win any more you realise how difficult that is. ‘But it was an incredible time and we feel so lucky in 2012 to have been able to win the FA Cup, then the Champions League, then the Euros with Spain, both of us scoring in the final. It was an incredible two or three months, probably the best summer in my life. ‘With time you get to realise how difficult that is in a playing career. To win one of those trophies is a lot, but having the chance to win those trophies together, it’s like a dream. We were riding a wave of positivity, of good football, and especially good results. It was incredible.’ Ever modest, Juan says ‘it was incredible’. For the Chelsea supporters in the stands, it was more often ‘he is incredible’. They said as much when they voted Mata the club’s Player of the Year for 2011/12, and again the following season, when it was joined on his mantelpiece by the Players’ Player of the Year award. Despite it being Mata's first time living abroad, there were no problems settling in England, on and off the pitch. According to Juan, that is because one goes hand in hand with the other. ‘I loved it,’ he replied emphatically, when asked how he found living in a different country for the first time. ‘As soon as I arrived in London I felt a great energy. It was positive from when I first arrived. ‘Of course, London is a great city. I loved my life in London, getting to know a different country, different culture, different language. A city with a lot of opportunities. ‘On the pitch, it worked perfectly from the first minute - I remember scoring on my debut. So it was a big change in my life, leaving Spain, leaving Valencia where I was living for four years, but I felt it was the right time and I’m so happy that I did. ‘My team-mates were great, we had a great dressing room. For example, in my case, Fernando Torres, and the captain and leaders - John Terry, Petr Cech, Frank Lampard. 'They were very helpful in the beginning and offered their help for anything I might have needed. With their help, and also with my willingness to discover London and settle in, it was a fairly quick adaptation.’ Among those team-mates he had support readily available in the form of what soon became a close community of Spanish players. There was the more experienced Fernando Torres, who had signed for Chelsea from Liverpool the previous January, Oriol Romeu arrived from Barcelona a few weeks before Juan in August 2011, and Cesar Azpilicueta would join them the following summer. ‘It was super important. First, to have Fernando; he was actually very important in the decision to go to Chelsea. He called me before when the interest was there and he told me how life was there, how the club wanted me and the coach. 'It made my decision easier. I had so much respect, admiration and love for Fernando as a player and a person. He was a great help. ‘Oriol arrived at the same time and he is one of the best humans I’ve met in my whole life, not only in football. It was fantastic to be there with him, to get to know such an amazing personality. We still speak a lot. 'It was definitely one of my positives at Chelsea to get to know Fernando better and get to know Oriol, and Azpi, who arrived later. ‘We were more than team-mates, we were friends. Of course, my relationship with Fernando had already begun before with the national team, but because of our time together at Chelsea we became close friends. 'I consider him one of my best friends in my career. He was older and he was more experienced. He was a very important player; he was always giving me advice and the others. He was very important for all of us and I learned so much from him. ‘I also already knew Azpi from the national team and the Under-21s and the younger generations, but again we made a strong relationship. ‘With Oriol, we were living in the same building in Battersea, so we were going to training and back in the same car together most of the time. I got to know his amazing family, he got to know mine. 'We used to watch football together, on Champions League nights. We used to have dinner together. On days off we would make plans together in London. We were friends and we spent so much time together. And I can tell you, with a guy like Ori, he is someone you want to spend time with because your day will improve if you are around him! ‘We found Spanish restaurants. The famous Cambio de Tercio on Old Brompton Road we used to go to a lot. Oriol also had friends who worked in restaurants in the east part of the city and doing Spanish guided tours. 'There are a lot of nationalities in London and a lot of Spanish people, plus we had a lot of visitors to watch games and things. So we were never bored! ‘The four of us are very good friends and I’m very grateful we spent so much time together, but we also integrated ourselves very good in the dressing room with all of the personalities and other cultures and nationalities. 'I think that was the key with winning the Champions League, the FA Cup and the Europa League, to have a great energy in the dressing room.’ Mata and Azpilicueta were relatively early in their careers when they joined Chelsea. What the latter went on to achieve, becoming Chelsea captain and winning every piece of silverware going at Stamford Bridge, was yet to be written. However, Mata confirms the attributes which made Azpi such a success were already apparent when he signed from Marseille in 2012. ‘He already had some experience in football, mainly in the Spanish and French leagues, but you could see already his determination. I think Azpi is a guy who has achieved what he has achieved because of his professionalism and his mind-set and his determination. 'On top of his qualities as a player, for me his key feature is his mind, and you could already see it in the beginning. ‘He had some trouble, having not as much game time as he wanted in the beginning, but he was very determined waiting for his chance and he got what he deserved. 'He had an incredible career at Chelsea, winning so many trophies, being the captain for some time. He’s a legend at the club and he got the recognition that he deserved because he committed 100 per cent to his profession.’ It was not just with his fellow players that Mata had a great relationship with at Chelsea. There is no mistaking the high regard he and the Blues supporters held each other in – and that bond has continued long after his own departure in January 2014. ‘I still get that feeling from Chelsea fans. I’m so grateful for the love they gave me. I understand it was a great time to be a Chelsea fan, winning the Champions League, winning the FA Cup and the Europa League. 'I was also just so lucky to be there at that time. It was a very important part of my life. ‘In your career you need talent, you need professionalism, you need consistency, but you also need luck to be in the right place at a certain time. I feel that I was at that time at Chelsea. 'I felt very good on the pitch, I felt very confident and I felt very grateful, because I could feel the support of the fans. ‘I felt that ever since I arrived. That pushed me to try to get better and better. Thankfully we could give them the reward that they deserved - trophies, goals and good football!’

Internationals: Neto scores as Quenda and Antwi make debuts
news.body_en: Pedro Neto went through the full range of emotions with Portugal on a crazy night in Wales, but it was his goal which guaranteed Portugal would finish top of their UEFA Nations League group, on the evening that Geovany Quenda and Genesis Antwi both represented their senior national teams for the first time. Neto started on the left wing for already qualified Portugal and was unlucky to only get his name on the score sheet once in the pouring rain in Cardiff. The visitors had taken an early lead through captain Bruno Fernandes, only to concede twice, when Neto side-footed in the equaliser shortly before half-time, setting them on course for the point they needed to guarantee top spot. The Chelsea man then came agonisingly close to a second by hitting the foot of the post, before Carlos Forbs did get the winner. However, in a match which had been fiercely contested throughout, Neto committed two fouls in the space of three minutes. He was booked for both of them, meaning his match came to an early end. Portugal held on against Wales for the remaining 14 minutes, helped by Quenda, who replaced Fernandes in the closing stages to make his senior international debut. They progress to the Nations League quarter-finals as group winners, with five victories from six games. That was one of two debuts for Chelsea players on Tuesday evening. The other was Academy graduate Antwi – currently impressing on loan at Strasbourg – who came on as a late substitute for Sweden in their 1-1 draw away to Poland. They also finish first in their group, earning promotion to the top tier of the Nations League. Neto and Quenda weren’t the only Blues in action for Portugal on Tuesday, with Academy midfielder Isaac Badu lining up for the country’s Under-18s in a home friendly against the USA earlier in the day. They claimed a 2-1 victory, with all three goals coming in the space of five frantic first-half minutes. Freddy Bernal, Landon Emenalo, Reggie Walsh and Chizaram Ezenwata all started for England Under-19s against Austria in qualification for next year’s European Championship. Walsh found the net with an instant reply after England had conceded early on and Bernal produced a series of strong saves. It wasn’t enough to prevent a 4-1 defeat, although the six points already accumulated were enough for England to progress to the third and final round of qualifying. In the younger age group, Reggie Watson captained England Under-17s to victory alongside fellow Chelsea midfielder Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli, with Josh Henry among the substitutes. They defeated Ukraine 3-0 to claim maximum points from this month’s European Championship qualifying round. Elsewhere, Alfie Osborne captained Scotland Under-19s once again, although they suffered their only defeat of the international window, falling 4-1 to Belgium. Jacob Hall was part of the USA Under-20s side which were beaten 2-1 by Paraguay in a home friendly.

news.title: Key talking points from Bompastor and Cuthbert's pre-Paris Saint-Germain press conference
news.body_en: Head coach Sonia Bompastor and captain Erin Cuthbert spoke to the media at Cobham on Tuesday, before Chelsea host Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Women's Champions League, and here are the main talking points from what they had to say. Chelsea head to Plough Lane for Wednesday evening's game in good spirits after beating Manchester City 1-0 last time out, going clear at the top of the Women's Super League table in the process. In Europe, the Blues remain unbeaten and are yet to concede a goal. Despite a 0-0 draw away to Hacken last week, Chelsea are within two points of the leaders in the league phase, but have fallen just outside of the top four and a guaranteed spot in the quarter-finals, without the need for an additional play-off tie. Bompastor: 'We’re feeling great. The Champions League is back. We love this competition and I think right now we are playing every three days. It's really busy, but it's really nice to be able to be back in the Champions League.' Cuthbert: 'Yeah, I feel good. I think, from a player’s perspective, we just want the next game in the Champions League to come, because we dropped points in the last game, and felt like we had a good performance and we just couldn't get the ball in the net. 'So we've had a look at that over the weekend. We've been analysing it. We obviously had a great game at the weekend, but now it's a chance to put things right tomorrow.' Bompastor: 'I think that's important, but these values from us are part of what we want to do when we come on the pitch. We want to come with confidence. We want to come with belief. 'I told my players, what is under our control is for us to be able to put in a good performance on the pitch and make sure we are able to win both the next games. We focus on the next one tomorrow against PSG, but it's under our control. 'I think if we win tomorrow we'll be again in a good position. So we are confident and we have the belief that we have enough quality to still finish in the top four in this competition.' Bompastor: 'I think it's probably not the right time for us to assess our season so far, in terms of we still have two games left in this block. We just want to continue with the quality we have shown on the pitch from the beginning of the season. 'We know who we are as a team, what we want to achieve together. We always have the right balance between having confidence, because we know the quality we have in the squad, but also being humble, because it's so early in the season and we haven’t achieved anything yet.' Cuthbert: 'Just what Sonia said, I'm very much of the opinion that we've won nothing yet. There are no trophies on the table yet. I think the only thing that has been really positive is we've put ourselves in a good position, and that's all it is. 'It's now how do we then look forward and try to win our remaining games in the Champions League to put ourselves in a good position. Obviously it's great to be back at the top of the WSL table, but the league is not won or lost based on the game on Saturday.' Bompastor: 'I always say that when you are strong defensively, it allows you to go really far in every competition you are competing in. If you want to win trophies, you need to make sure you have that and you are able to score goals. 'So right now, the defensive aspects have been something really good for us. The whole team is putting a lot of effort on the pitch to protect the goal. As a mentality in the team, we don't want to concede a goal. That's why it's important for everyone to make the efforts on the pitch, and I'm really pleased with everyone's contribution to that. 'It gives the team the confidence we need. We know right now most of the things we are doing in terms of the defensive aspects, we are doing them well individually, but as a team as well. So I think it goes with the players having clarity on what they need to do on the pitch, but also being on the same page to do those things in the right moments.' Bompastor: 'It's really good news for her. We know her really well. We decided to loan her to Nottingham Forest to get minutes on the pitch. Every week I'm getting the reports from her performances and I know she's doing well over there. So it's credit to her, to all the hard work she has put in on the pitch, and it will be an amazing experience for her as well.'

news.title: Bompastor Press Conference 🎙️
Training gallery: Back to it at Cobham
Bompastor updates on Buchanan, Dragoni, Malard and Matsukubo ahead of PSG
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor revealed that she will be without a striker for Wednesday’s UEFA Women’s Champions League tie with Paris Saint-Germain but has gained two players who have recovered from injury, while providing the latest on the returns of several players who have been missing recently. At either end of the pitch for Chelsea, centre-forward Melvine Malard and centre-back Kadeisha Buchanan both had to be replaced in the first half of Saturday’s 1-0 win over Manchester City, which sent the Blues top of the Women’s Super League table. It was a heavy cost for an important victory, and Bompastor confirmed that Malard will be ruled out by the issue she suffered at Stamford Bridge. ‘Melvine picked up an injury in the last game against Man City so she won’t be available for the two games left during this block,’ said the Blues head coach in her pre-match press conference ahead of the meeting with PSG. ‘So we will assess her during the international break and see where she is, but she picked up an injury in her hamstring. ‘I think we need to assess her in ten days, so probably we will have a better picture during the international break to see exactly how long she will be out.’ However, there was better news on Buchanan, as well as the potential imminent returns to the pitch of summer signings Giulia Dragoni and Manaka Matsukubo, who both missed Saturday’s game. ‘Kadeisha is fine after the weekend, she is available for the game tomorrow. She could train normally today,’ Bompastor continued. ‘Giulia is back in the squad. Manaka won’t be in the squad tomorrow, but she is not far from being in the group and training with us again.’ Bompastor had previously confirmed that neither Lauren James nor Naomi Girma would be able to return in time for Wednesday’s Champions League meeting with Paris Saint-Germain at Plough Lane, but provided an update on their progress. ‘As I said on Melvine, Lauren won’t be available for the next two games and we’ll have to assess her again during the international break to see exactly about the timeline. ‘LJ is doing well. I think for this block she won’t be available, but we will update everyone after the international break about how long she will take to come back again. ‘Naomi is still rehabbing. She is progressing well. She will stay with us during the international break and the plan is for her to be back probably after the international break.’

news.title: Sandy Baltimore grateful for Paris education but not looking back
news.body_en: Sandy Baltimore discussed how Paris and Paris Saint-Germain helped shape her both as a footballer and a person, but is only looking to the future with Chelsea now as she prepares to face her former club in west London. Chelsea Women continue our unbeaten UEFA Women’s Champions League campaign on Wednesday evening when we host Paris Saint-Germain at Plough Lane, looking to register our third win. For Baltimore, it is a fixture which will have added significance. She is preparing to line up against Paris Saint-Germain as an opponent for the first time, having won the league and three cups with PSG, as well as reaching the Champions League final in 2017. The French international was born and raised in the Parisian suburbs and began her professional career with the club, spending nine years representing Paris Saint-Germain before moving to England to join Chelsea in 2024. ‘I grew up in Paris, I was born there, so I grew up with PSG. They were my first team and it was good over there,’ Baltimore tells us ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League showdown. ‘I learned a lot of things about football and me personally in Paris, about women, about growing up, about developing as a person. I started football in school with the boys, just playing football outside with some friends, just chill. ‘I was 15 years old when I joined PSG, I was with the Under-19s straight away. Then after I trained with the Under-19s, I joined the first team at 16 or 17. ‘When you want to grow up more, it was good I joined PSG when I was younger. Then after, you just work every day, you learn, because they are also good players there. So I learned a lot. ‘It was good when we won the league. I was so happy because it was my first trophy, because I’m from Paris and I played for PSG, and you have also your family, your friends. You have a lot of things, so you feel good after that.’ That meant it was a big step for Baltimore when she took the chance to leave Paris and PSG behind for London and Chelsea, moving away from her home city and club for the first time. Although there have been challenges along the way, she insists it was not a difficult switch to make. ‘Honestly, at the beginning for me it wasn't difficult, because it was my objective to grow, to change, to take another opportunity to progress in my career and as a woman. So I was happy to come here. ‘The leagues in England and France are different, especially the intensity and physicality, so I think I learn a lot because Chelsea is a good team, we have good players. So you work every day and then I progress also. It's good. ‘This season, at the beginning, I didn't play too much. When you are a player, you're a little bit frustrated to not play, but I have a big mentality and I also work with a mentality coach, so he helped me a lot. ‘Also, I don't talk too much, but I work hard every day. I learn and I just keep going because I don't want to give up. I never give up. So for me, it's important to keep going, go forward and then just show your quality on the pitch.’ Now, her focus is fully on the Blues and gaining another important three points in this season’s Champions League on Wednesday, which could potentially move us into first place in the standings, if results elsewhere go our way. Chelsea head into the match on a high, too, after going clear at the top of the Women’s Super League table with a 1-0 win over Manchester City at the weekend, courtesy of Baltimore’s stunning strike in first-half added time. ‘It was important because we know how the table looks, it’s really tight,’ she added. ‘So it was important for us to win this game because every week it's hard to win. ‘But we did and we were so happy. We stuck together and I scored and I tried to help the team, so I was happy. I think we go forward with more confidence, because last week against Man City we played well. ‘But I think it's different, because the Champions League is the Champions League. Everyone wants to win that. I think every team looks different when it’s the Champions League, so you have to prepare for that and you’ve got to be on your best game.’

news.title: Internationals: Estevao nets and assists in big Brazil win
news.body_en: Estevao Willian scored for Brazil and registered two assists as they thrashed Singapore 7-0 in a friendly on Tuesday. Vinicius Junior had already netted a brace when Estevao unselfishly teed him up in the 21st minute so the Real Madrid striker could complete an early hat-trick. The Chelsea attacker then set up Endrick to extend Brazil's advantage, and had a goal of his own ruled out for a foul in the build-up shortly before the break. Estevao did then get in on the act early in the second half, firing home with the aid of a deflection from a half-cleared free-kick. Estevao, who started on the right side of Brazil's attack, was replaced on 70 minutes to a standing ovation inside the National Stadium in Singapore. He now has seven international goals to his name in 16 caps.

news.title: Dramatic Palmer strike voted your favourite late Chelsea winner!
news.body_en: Cole Palmer’s 101st-minute goal against Manchester United in 2024 has been voted by Blues fans on the Chelsea Official App as their favourite late winner scored at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League. It was two current members of our squad vying for the crown, which began with our quarter-final vote last week, as Palmer took on Estevao Willian’s late strike against Liverpool a year ago. And it was Palmer who emerged victorious, receiving 62 per cent of the votes cast on the Chelsea Official App. The attacker had only just equalised from the penalty spot - making it 3-3 - when he collected a short corner and fired a shot goalwards that took a small deflection on its way into the back of the Matthew Harding net. It sparked absolute pandemonium in the stands and on the pitch as a dramatic three points was won when it looked like we would leave with nothing. The second-latest winning goal in Premier League history is a worthy winner of the award. Congratulations, Cole!

news.title: Squad debutant among six Blues called up by England Women
news.body_en: Chelsea Women will be represented by no fewer than six players in the England Women squad, including a first call-up for Academy graduate Katie Cox. The Lionesses face Ukraine in a two-legged qualifying play-off for the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup, with those matches to be played on 2 and 5 December. Hannah Hampton, Lucy Bronze, Keira Walsh and Lexi Potter - who made her own senior international debut during the last window - all retain their places in Sarina Wiegman's squad, while striker Aggie Beever-Jones is recalled to the group. Following Potter's first call-up in October, now it is the turn of another homegrown Blue, Cox, who has impressed on loan at Nottingham Forest this season. Having represented her country through the age groups from Under-16s to Under-23s, the young goalkeeper has now been named in the senior squad for the first time. Having already recorded a resounding 8-1 aggregate win over Greece in the first round of the play-offs, England would book their place in Brazil for next summer's World Cup with another victory over Ukraine.

news.title: Matchday Unseen | Man City 🎥
Flying full-back your Chelsea Women Player of the Month
news.body_en: Chelsea Women completed a brilliant October with a 100 per cent record and supporters on the Chelsea Official App have chosen their standout performer. The Blues triumphed in all four of our matches across all competitions last month, with a trio of London derby wins against West Ham United, Tottenham Hotspur and Crystal Palace in the Women's Super League combined with a 2-0 victory over Roma at home in the UEFA Women's Champions League. Ellie Carpenter's form across those four fixtures earned her 44 per cent of the fans' votes on the Chelsea Official App to seal her status as our October Player of the Month. The Australian international started all our WSL games, finding the net twice in the big win over Spurs, before coming off the bench to score the opening goal against Roma. Lauren James wasn't far behind, taking 34 per cent of the votes in the poll, ahead of third-placed Melvine Malard on 12 per cent. There is little time for Carpenter and her team-mates to reflect, though, with the Blues' attention now firmly fixed on our next game against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday evening, before returning to WSL duties with an away trip to Liverpool on Saturday.

news.title: Internationals: Jashayde Greenwood nets for England Under-18s
news.body_en: A number of Chelsea youngsters were in international action during the latest break, with representatives featuring for both England Under-18s and Under-20s, as well as Portugal Under-20s. England Under-18s concluded their trio of friendlies during this window with a narrow 2-1 defeat to Switzerland. Gabriel Sambou and Jashayde Greenwood started for the Young Lions, with Greenwood scoring England's only goal of the game. England Under-20s were victorious in their match against Portugal, meanwhile. Jesse Derry started the 2-1 win, while Shim Mheuka and Olutayo Subuloye were on the bench. The former came on in the 63rd minute. Cobham Next Gen’s Leo Cardoso also featured in that game, introduced in the 79th minute for Portugal Under-20s. As the international break draws to a close, several young Chelsea players will be taking part in their final national team matches of 2026 on Tuesday, with as many as ten Blues in action. We will keep you updated as to how they get on.

news.title: Cole Palmer: My Football Firsts
news.body_en: Cole Palmer is the latest Chelsea player to share his early footballing memories by answering our series of quickfire questions. The Blues No10 recalls his start in the game in the Manchester City youth system before moving south to Chelsea in 2023... What was the first game you attended? Manchester United against Burnley. What was the first team you played for? What’s the first piece of footballing advice you remember getting? Who was your first friend in football? Lewis Fiorini. He’s still playing for Stockport. Who was the first team-mate you roomed with on an away trip? Was it Morgan Rogers? No, that was Lewis as well. Who was your professional debut against? It was for Man City in the League Cup, against Burnley. What was the first professional goal you scored? In the League Cup for Man City again, when we beat Wycombe. When was the first time you were recognised in public? I can’t remember, but it probably would have been around Manchester. What was your first emotion after signing for Chelsea? It feels like a long time ago, but I was just happy.

news.title: Chelsea Women vs Paris Saint-Germain: How to watch, TV channel, kick-off time, date
news.body_en: Chelsea host Paris Saint-Germain in west London on Wednesday as we look to continue our unbeaten run in this season's UEFA Women's Champions League. The Blues are yet to concede a goal in Europe after four games of the league phase, with two wins and two draws to our name so far. That leaves us in fifth place, but only two points behind leaders Lyon and Barcelona. Here is everything you need to know about how to watch Chelsea Women against Paris Saint-Germain, including kick-off time and how to follow the action on official Chelsea channels. Chelsea Women's game against PSG takes place on Wednesday 18 November at Plough Lane, with kick-off scheduled for 8pm UK time. The match will be shown live in the UK on Disney+. As always, you can follow minute-by-minute updates in our Chelsea Women vs Paris Saint-Germain Match Centre on the Chelsea Official App and website. You can also follow through Chelsea Women’s social media channels on X, Facebook and Instagram. Chelsea have a 100 per cent record from our two home matches in this season's Champions League, opening our campaign with a 1-0 win over Austria Vienna, before beating Roma 2-0. A pair of goalless draws away at Lyon and Hacken mean we remain undefeated in Europe, alongside topping the Women's Super League on the domestic front, following Saturday's victory against Manchester City. Paris Saint-Germain lost their own undefeated record in this season's Champions League in their last match, when they were beaten 2-1 at home by Bayern Munich. Before that, like Chelsea, PSG had drawn their two away trips with Real Madrid and Man City, either side of thrashing Leuven 5-0 in France. This will be the fifth match between Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain in the Women's Champions League, with the most recent meeting coming in the 2022/23 group stage. On that occasion, Millie Bright's solitary goal gave the Blues a narrow victory in the French capital. Back in London, Sam Kerr opened the scoring just before half-time, before a second-half brace by Lauren James secured a more comprehensive 3-0 win for Chelsea.
